submitted.rationale: All three measured compositions gave cathodic (negative) photocurrent, which fits p-type Cu-containing oxides. Index 17 (Bi 0.20 / Cu 0.80) had the least negative value (-1.6e-7 A), so it has the highest signed merit.

rejected.reason: CuBi2O4 (Bi 0.667): -9.9e-7 A, the strongest cathodic current, which is the worst for a photoanode
Bi 0.83: -4.4e-7 A, still cathodic and lower than index 17

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts CuBi2O4 (mp-505042) on the hull, so a phase-pure region is expected near Bi=0.667 (index 6). MEGNet's ~0 eV HSE gap is uninformative because it misses the known ~1.5-1.8 eV experimental gap of this Cu2+ d9 compound. CuBi2O4 absorbs at 2.72 eV.

Support: MEGNet HSE gap of 2.34 eV for α-Bi2O3 (mp-23262) is below the 2.72 eV photon energy, so the Bi-rich n-type Bi2O3 phase should absorb and could give anodic photocurrent. CuBi2O4 (index 6) gave a cathodic current, so move to the Bi-rich end (index 7, Bi=0.83).

Uninformative to weakly against: MACE puts this CuO polymorph (mp-14549) 0.18 eV/atom above the hull, and in any case CuO is usually p-type. But the Cu-rich end (index 17) is the only unexplored region and the GP suggests it. Both Bi-rich measurements were cathodic, so measure index 17 to explore.
